My teaching philosophy

Bridging the gap between learned knowledge and applied knowledge

I have studied in different education systems and worked in research and development, where knowing a fact is never enough: you have to be able to use it. That is how I teach. Students first build a core understanding of each concept, then learn to apply it, so that problems stop feeling like puzzles to memorise and start to make sense.

Step 1

Learned knowledge

What the textbook and syllabus teach: definitions, rules, formulas.

Step 2 · The bridge

Core concept understanding

Why it works, how ideas connect, and where it shows up in the real world.

Step 3

Applied knowledge

Solving new problems with confidence, in exams and beyond them.

Beyond the syllabus

Character shapes how a child solves problems

Alongside academics, I believe character development is essential. The way a student approaches a problem comes from their core personality, and that personality shapes who they become in real life. That is why every class also builds the mindset behind the answers.

Curiosity Asking "why?" before "what's the answer?"
Perseverance Staying with a hard problem instead of giving up
Independent thinking Finding their own path to a solution
